This is a strategic transition. Moving from a full-time employee mindset to a "portfolio career" (juggling multiple contracts) requires viewing yourself not as an employee, but as a business offering specific solutions. This aligns perfectly with your desire to explore different "ways of life" in the industry while maintaining the freedom to pivot.

Given your diverse background—ranging from embedded defense systems to full-stack web development and military leadership—you are well-positioned to act as a "Fractional Engineer."

Here is a strategy to capitalize on your LinkedIn Premium subscription to find those 2-3 flexible, small-to-medium contracts, integrating perspectives from the startup world, the agency model, and the independent consultant community.

1. The "Fractional" Positioning Strategy

To attract the right kind of client (small business owners who value results over hours), you need to reframe your profile. You aren't "looking for a job"; you are offering a specialized service.

  • The Headline: Shift from a title to a value proposition.
    • Draft Idea: "Fractional Software Engineer | Embedded C++ & Full Stack Systems | Helping Startups Scale & Prototype"
  • The "About" Section: Use the "natural intuition" angle. .
  • The "Open to Work" Feature: Set this strictly to Contract and Part-time. With Premium, you can signal this to recruiters while keeping it subtle if you prefer, though for independent work, being loud about it is better.

2. Targeting Diverse "Industry Ecosystems"

To get 2-3 distinct contracts, you should diversify the types of work to avoid burnout. Based on your resume, here are three distinct "communities" you should target using LinkedIn Sales Navigator (or advanced search):

A. The "Hard Tech" & IoT Makers (Leveraging C++ & Embedded)

  • The Vibe: Inventors, hardware startups, and prototypers. They often need someone who understands the "intricacies" of hardware-software integration but can't afford a full-time senior engineer.

B. The "Digital Transformation" Sector (Leveraging Full Stack & .NET)

  • The Vibe: established small businesses or non-technical industries (Logistics, Agriculture, Retail) that need their internal tools modernized.
  • . This screams "ROI" to business owners.

  • Target: Companies in the Midwest (Des Moines/Ankeny area or remote) that have clunky internal software. They value stability and don't care when you work, as long as the tool works.

C. The "EdTech" & Training Niche (Leveraging M.A.T. & Leadership)

  • .

3. Tactical Use of LinkedIn Premium

Don't just apply to posted jobs (which are often flooded). Use the "Hidden Job Market" approach common among successful freelancers.

  • InMail Strategy (The "Sniper" Approach):
    • Search for Founders, CTOs, or Engineering Managers at companies with 1-50 employees.

I have some capacity for fractional work (embedded or full-stack) and love helping smaller teams ship faster without the overhead of a full-time hire. Would you be open to a 10-minute chat to see if I can take anything off your plate?"

4. Structuring for Efficiency & Low Commitment

You mentioned wanting to allocate time efficiently and the ability to leave with 2 weeks' notice.

  • Contract Clauses: Since you have an LLC/website (arognes.com), draft a standard Service Agreement that explicitly states a 14-day termination clause for convenience. Small companies usually appreciate this flexibility too—it lowers their risk.
  • Asynchronous Default: When interviewing, emphasize that your "intuition for learning" allows you to work autonomously. as a benefit: "I do my deep work early in the morning/late at night," ensuring they focus on output, not presence.

3. The Flexible Service Agreement (MSA)

Since you are setting up an LLC and want the ability to leave with just 2 weeks' notice (rather than being locked into 6-12 month deliverables), your contract needs to be explicit.

You should draft a Master Services Agreement (MSA). This acts as the "umbrella" contract covering legal terms, while individual "Statements of Work" (SOW) cover the specific tasks.

Here are the 3 Critical Clauses you must include to protect your freedom:

A. The "Termination for Convenience" Clause

This is the most important clause for your specific request. Standard contracts often require "cause" to fire or quit. You want the right to leave for any reason.

  • Draft Language: "Either Party may terminate this Agreement or any active Statement of Work at any time, with or without cause, upon providing fourteen (14) days' prior written notice to the other Party."
  • Why this works: It gives you the "escape hatch" you requested. If a big opportunity comes up, or if you just want to pivot, you are only bound for two weeks.

B. The "Independent Contractor" Status

To ensure you stay "fractional" and don't get treated like an employee (which limits your ability to have multiple clients), this must be clear.

  • Draft Language: "Contractor is an independent contractor, not an employee. Contractor has the sole right to control and direct the means, manner, and method by which the Services are performed. Contractor shall provide their own equipment and is free to perform services for other clients."
  • Why this works: It reinforces your autonomy. It allows you to work your own hours (e.g., late nights or early mornings) as long as the job gets done.

C. Intellectual Property (IP) Transfer "Upon Payment"

This protects you from doing work and not getting paid.

  • Draft Language: "Rights to any Deliverables or Intellectual Property created by Contractor shall transfer to Client only upon full payment of all Fees associated with said Deliverables."
  • Why this works: If a startup runs out of money or a client ghosts you, you legally own the code until they pay up.

Here is a simple, flexible Master Services Agreement (MSA) tailored for your specific needs: keeping your freedom, protecting your IP, and allowing you to exit with 2 weeks' notice.

Note: I am an AI, not a lawyer. This document is a template based on standard industry practices for freelance software engineers. You should review this with a local business attorney or legal professional in Iowa to ensure it fully protects your specific LLC.

MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT

Effective Date: [Date] Between: Contractor: [Your LLC Name OR Austin Rognes], located at Ankeny, Iowa ("Contractor") Client: [Client Company Name], located at [Client Address] ("Client")

1. Services

Contractor agrees to provide software engineering and consulting services ("Services") as defined in specific Statements of Work (SOW) signed by both parties. Each SOW shall be subject to the terms of this Agreement. In the event of a conflict between this Agreement and an SOW, the terms of the SOW shall govern regarding specific deliverables or dates, but this Agreement shall govern regarding legal terms.

2. Independent Contractor Status

2.1 Autonomy: Contractor is an independent contractor, not an employee of Client. Contractor has the sole right to control and direct the means, manner, and method by which the Services are performed. 2.2 Non-Exclusivity: Client acknowledges that Contractor creates software for other clients. Nothing in this Agreement restricts Contractor from providing similar services to third parties, provided that Contractor does not breach the Confidentiality obligations herein. 2.3 Tools & Equipment: Contractor shall provide their own equipment, software, and tools necessary to perform the Services (e.g., computers, development environments).

3. Compensation & Payment

3.1 Fees: Client agrees to pay Contractor the fees set forth in the applicable SOW. 3.2 Invoicing: Contractor will invoice Client [Weekly/Bi-Weekly/Monthly]. 3.3 Payment Terms: Invoices are due within [15 or 30] days of receipt. Late payments may incur a late fee of 1.5% per month. 3.4 Expenses: Reasonable, pre-approved expenses incurred by Contractor in performing the Services will be reimbursed by Client.

4. Term & Termination

4.1 Term: This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues until terminated. 4.2 Termination for Convenience: Either Party may terminate this Agreement or any active SOW at any time, for any reason or no reason, upon providing fourteen (14) days’ prior written notice to the other Party. 4.3 Payment Upon Termination: Upon termination, Client shall pay Contractor for all Services performed and expenses incurred up to the effective date of termination.

5. Intellectual Property (IP)

5.1 Work Product: Subject to Section 5.2, all code, documentation, and deliverables created specifically for Client under this Agreement ("Work Product") shall be considered "work made for hire" and owned by Client. 5.2 Transfer Upon Payment: Notwithstanding the foregoing, the assignment of ownership rights in the Work Product is expressly conditioned upon Client’s full payment of all fees associated with said Work Product. Until full payment is received, Contractor retains all rights, title, and interest in the Work Product. 5.3 Background IP: Contractor retains ownership of any pre-existing code, libraries, or tools ("Background IP") incorporated into the Work Product. Contractor grants Client a non-exclusive, perpetual, royalty-free license to use such Background IP as necessary to utilize the Work Product.

6. Confidentiality

Both parties agree to keep confidential all non-public information disclosed by the other party ("Confidential Information"). Contractor will not disclose Client’s trade secrets or proprietary code to third parties without permission. Client will not disclose Contractor’s proprietary rates or methods.

7. Warranties & Liability

7.1 Warranty: Contractor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner. 7.2 Limitation of Liability: To the maximum extent permitted by law, Contractor’s total liability to Client for any damages arising out of this Agreement shall be limited to the total fees paid by Client to Contractor under the applicable SOW during the three (3) months prior to the claim. In no event shall Contractor be liable for lost profits or consequential damages.

8. General

8.1 Governing Law: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of Iowa. 8.2 Entire Agreement: This Agreement constitutes the entire understanding between the parties.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Agreement as of the Effective Date.
